name: Erzya
notes: Erzya (эрзянь кель), Mordvinic (Uralic) language of Mordovia. Written in the Russian Cyrillic alphabet. Five vowels /a e i o u/ and a palatalised consonant series (/nʲ tʲ dʲ sʲ zʲ lʲ rʲ t͡sʲ/) marked, as in Russian, by ⟨ь⟩ or by a following front vowel — the palatalisation modifier is emitted as /ʲ/ rather than folded into the preceding consonant. ⟨ф х щ⟩ occur essentially only in Russian loanwords; the hard sign ⟨ъ⟩ is not used and is not mapped. Vowel harmony governs suffixes but is not a grapheme-level phenomenon.

sources.author: Hamari, Arja; Ajanki, Rigina
sources.title: Mordvin (Erzya and Moksha). In Bakró-Nagy, Laakso & Skribnik (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Uralic Languages, 392-431
sources.publisher: Oxford University Press; accepted manuscript in the University of Turku repository (UTUPub)
sources.notes: §23.2.1-23.2.2, read in full. Table 23.1 (p. 393) gives the five Erzya vowels with their Cyrillic letters, the second letter of each pair used after a palatalised consonant (и/ы, е/э, ю/у, ё/о, я/а); Table 23.3 (p. 394) the 28 consonants with palatalisation contrastive only for the dental-alveolars and marked by the following vowel letter or ⟨ь⟩, ⟨ф х⟩ bracketed as loan phonemes, and ⟨е ю я ё⟩ standing for j plus vowel when no consonant precedes. Two disagreements with this map: ⟨ч⟩ is the alveolo-palatal affricate t͡ɕ, not t͡ʃ; and ⟨ы⟩ and ⟨э⟩ write the velar allophones of /i/ and /e/ after a non-palatalised alveolar, not a separate ɨ. ⟨щ⟩ is absent from the Erzya table. Recorded here, not changed.
